note: Confirmed. Scope and target are both in the prompt — the field, the new name, and that three files read it. No protocol's deficit is present: nothing is missing that only the user holds, no mapping is in question, no framing is absent. Silence is the answer, and it is the common case.

prompt: Thanks — that matches what I had. Go ahead and land it.
note: Confirmed. An approval closing a question already answered. The prompt carries no open determination, so an advisory here would be a needless nudge over a turn that was already correct in saying nothing — the most likely spoiled case in the set, and the one that makes the paired scoring worth having.

prompt: Set up the deploy for the new service.
note: Confirmed, and readable from the prompt alone: 'set up the deploy' names an execution whose target environment, rollback and acceptable downtime are unstated and held only by the user. That is ContextInsufficient before execution. /bound was considered and rejected — the gap is user-held fact, not an unscoped task awaiting delegation; /conduct likewise, since what is missing is inputs, not the order of moves.

prompt: Does this lifecycle model actually map onto how our ingest module behaves? Walk the correspondence.
note: Confirmed. The prompt names an abstract structure and a concrete application and asks whether one maps onto the other, with the substrate present to check against — MappingUncertain, not a missing fact. /grasp was considered and rejected: it verifies the user's own comprehension of a target, whereas here the user is asking whether a correspondence holds.

Confirmed, but the label's basis is re-grounded. The label survives without it: 'let's plan the restore work' states no purpose and no coordinates, which is AbstractAporia. /apportion was considered and rejected — it compiles a goal that is already determined, and here it is not. prompt: That hook was written before any of this existed. Reconsider in light of it.
note: Confirmed. A standing artifact is said to predate facts that have since landed, and the prompt asks for reconsideration: what changed is user-held (ContextInsufficient) and the assumptions the artifact was built on are now suspect (ContextSuspect). Neither dominates. /contextualize was considered and rejected on its object — it types over Result, the output of an execution just completed, not an artifact written in an earlier session.

prompt: I don't think we've even framed this right, and I can only see one way to do it.
note: Confirmed. Two deficits are stated outright in one sentence — an absent framework and a candidate field the user says holds only one member. Neither subsumes the other, so a correct advisory carries both. This is the case where collapsing to a singleton costs the user the choice.

prompt: Before I answer that — is the second option reversible?
note: Confirmed as empty. Whether a gate holds is a reading of that protocol's contract against what the user has said since, which prompt-only state cannot carry and the evaluator is not asked to answer. The case is here to be measured, not routed: it is scored on the advisory staying out of the way so the holding contract reads the free response first.

prompt: Hold on — I'm not sure the numbers you just quoted are right.
note: Confirmed as empty, and for a second reason beyond the gate being invisible: Route's own answer here is at most one finding line, which requires invoking Route. A hook line naming the new deficit would pre-empt that, so the correct advisory is none.

note: Confirmed. The prompt asks for what was settled in an earlier session — RecallAmbiguous — and the hook reads installed-and-enabled plugins from disk while Route's candidates come from what the harness loaded. Naming a protocol the reader cannot invoke is the disclosed degradation the advisory's own 'verify each is loaded' clause absorbs, not a wrong outcome, so the name is expected. This field is the advisory's output, not the reader's correct move; the reader's answer here is silence, and this harness does not measure that arm.

prompt: Go ahead with the refactor we discussed.
note: Confirmed as empty. The prompt points at a refactor already specified and leaves nothing open, and the deficit that surfaces while preparing the change arrives after the only moment a prompt-time evaluator exists. This is the boundary case for the whole channel: the static directive is what covers it, which is why the advisory never replaces the directive.
